description: AI agents go head-to-head against each other to compete on the best PnL they can obtain. Each agent gets their own simulated account and their trades are tracked and stored in a MySQL database. Incoming data feed from ProjectX TopstepX API is distributed to all agents via Kafka. Each agent has a hand crafted personality, from yolo trader to calculated momentum trader. Each model selected has function tooling capabilities and can do one of four functions: get available contracts, get historical data for contract, get portfolio, and open/close position.

A backtest-driven Monte Carlo simulator that finds the prop-firm challenge configuration — strategy, risk-to-reward, and position sizing — with the best statistical odds of passing, then maximizing payouts once funded. It ingests 5-minute NQ/MNQ futures bars and backtests three intraday strategies (Opening Range Breakout, Mean Reversion, Trend Continuation) to extract real win rates and winner/loser distributions, then bootstraps thousands of Monte Carlo equity paths against the asymmetric $3K-target / $2K-drawdown account rules. Top configurations are independently re-validated with backtesting.py and rendered as EV breakeven curves, 3D pass-rate surfaces, and challenge/funded-phase payout heatmaps.

A production marketing site for a Pueblo, Colorado home-remodeling company, built on React 19, TypeScript, and rolldown-vite with TailwindCSS v4 and shadcn/ui. Its centerpiece is an interactive blueprint viewer that renders real project floorplans as hand-tagged SVG layers — structure, dimensions, details, and labels — each independently toggleable and explorable with zoom and pan. An animated hero cycles room types with a motion/react text loop, while service galleries, image carousels, and a masonry wall of real before/after photos sit alongside testimonials aggregated from Google and Facebook reviews. Fully responsive with light/dark theming, smooth scrolling, SEO/Open Graph metadata, and SPA routing, deployed on Netlify.

A bridge add-on that exposes NinjaTrader 8 — an otherwise GUI-only desktop trading platform — as a programmable REST API with real-time SSE and WebSocket streaming. The C# add-on hosts endpoints on port 5000 for accounts, positions, orders, executions, round-trip trades, instruments, quotes, and historical OHLCV bars, alongside live market-data, order, and account-event streams and bracket/OCO order placement. Ships with a Python CLI and client library, and runs in Docker.

A full-stack algorithmic trading engine for TopstepX, Topstep's funded-account evaluation platform. A NestJS backend streams live market and account data over SignalR, runs event-driven trading strategies, and relays real-time updates to the client over Socket.IO. The Next.js dashboard tracks daily growth against the profit target and max-loss limit, live P/L, trade distribution by sector, and best/worst trades, charted with TradingView lightweight-charts. Fully containerized with Docker Compose.

A Dockerized environment that runs NinjaTrader — a Windows-only futures trading platform — natively on Linux through the Wine compatibility layer. It packages a Wine prefix, the .NET/WPF runtime, Xvfb, and automated login into a reproducible image, exposing the desktop app through both a browser-based noVNC view and a native X11 display mode. Handles Tradovate brokerage authentication so the full trading platform runs headless in a container.
Created an npm package for the public to use that extends the Leaflet Path class. This allows for smooth geodesic (Great Circle) curves from a source coordinate to a destination coordinate.
